# CRITIQUE-01 — Milestone visual review

**Reviewed:** 2026-07-26
**Build:** working tree at `c3f17ca` (clean)
**Frames:** `docs/review/` — 11 stills at 1440×900, tier 2, generated by `node tools/shoot.mjs`
**Rubric:** `docs/VISUAL_RUBRIC.md` §3 (scoring), §4 (failure modes), §6 (contract constraints)

---

## 0. Scope, honesty, and what this review could not do

### 0.1 No reference imagery was available

**I did not perform a side-by-side comparison against *My Universe – My Baby*.** Outbound HTTPS is blocked in this container; every image host in Appendix A returns 403 at the proxy. `docs/reference/` is empty. **I have never seen a frame of the reference title.** Every score below is against the *written* 1/3/5 anchors in §3 and the numbered failure-mode checklist in §4, and nothing else. The §5 blind A/B protocol was **not run** and cannot be run from this environment. The verdict in §4 of this document is therefore an inference from the rubric's own textual description of the reference, explicitly flagged as such.

### 0.2 The known black-polygon bug is excluded

A large black polygon (the light shaft) occludes part or all of eight of the eleven frames. **I am not reporting it** — another agent owns it. Where it prevented assessment I say so and score nothing on that basis. Two exceptions, which are *separate* bugs that happen to also produce black or empty frames, are reported below with independent root-cause evidence (D1, D2).

### 0.3 Categories I could not assess

- **C12 (Particle & FX)** — **not scored.** Zero particles are visible in any of the eleven frames, including `21-bath-foam`, which explicitly requests `foam: 0.9, bubbles: true`. I cannot distinguish "not emitting" from "occluded by the black polygon," so I decline to score it. The absence is filed as a defect (D14) regardless.
- **C7 (Animation)** — **scored provisionally.** Stills cannot show motion. I scored it from two things stills *can* show (pose invariance across mood states) plus one code check, and I flag it as provisional in the table.

### 0.4 One hard-constraint violation, measured

`tools/shoot.mjs` reports render stats at the end of each run:

- Batch 1 (play → bath → sleep): **`calls: 288`**, 291,868 tris, 265 textures, 203 programs
- Batch 2 (play → dress → play): **`calls: 527`**, 536,706 tris

`CONTRACTS.md` line 18: *"Keep draw calls under ~180."* The build is 1.6× over on a cold path and **2.9× over after cycling activities**. The near-doubling between batches, with triangle count also doubling, is the signature of activity `dispose()` not releasing what `build()` created. This is a contract violation, not a taste judgement.

## 1. Per-shot critique

### `01-room-wide` — establishing shot, `play` / `wide` / day

**What works.** This is the best thing in the build and it is not close. The architectural shell is genuinely built, not faked: skirting board with a real section, a window with reveal depth and a hung curtain, bunting strung across two walls, three framed pictures with visible frame depth and a mat, a wall shelf carrying books / teddy / stacking ring, a wall clock with a bezel and hands, a chest of drawers with drawer reveals and knobs, a wire laundry basket, a changing mat with a rolled towel, a piped pouf with a top button, a child's chair, a low table, two stools, a rug, and a toy set (drum, xylophone, ball, blocks, balloon). Floor planks are staggered with varied lengths and directional grain. **Every prop casts a shadow** — this clears §4 #35, which the rubric's own calibration set failed. There is a real value range: true dark under the shelf and behind the chest, true bright on the sunlit rug. **§4 #101 (compressed value range) is resolved and should be protected.** The colour story — lilac wall / honey floor / dusty-pink rug — is coherent and deliberate.

**What is wrong.**

1. **The baby is naked.** No diaper, no top, nothing. In the hero establishing frame. `Baby.setOutfit()` has seven slots and not one is populated in the default state. This single fact makes the frame unshippable.
2. **The baby is ~7% of frame height and reads as an incidental prop.** The eye lands on the chest of drawers (brightest, highest-contrast mass) and then the shelf. §4 #47, #118. The subject is not the subject.
3. **The balloon is a solid glossy resin teardrop, point-down, larger than the baby's torso**, sitting directly in front of his chest. Its "string" is a 1–2px black line ending in mid-air on the rug with no anchor, no curve, no slack. An inflated balloon's neck is at the *bottom* — the shape is inverted relative to its tether. §4 #14, #78.
4. **The rug is a flat disc.** Hard elliptical edge against the floor, no pile thickness at the rim, no fringe, no ruck, no fold, no perimeter contact shadow. §4 #83.
5. **Everything is perfectly level and axis-aligned.** All three picture frames dead level and parallel to the wall. Shelf level. Chest square to the wall. Changing mat square. Towel roll square. Not one object a degree off cardinal. §4 #8, #74, #135.
6. **Clutter is a tidy arc of blocks.** `Room.clutter()` is doing the literal minimum. Nothing half-off a surface, nothing overflowing the basket, no blanket trailing, no book face-down, no sock. §4 #74, #81, #82.
7. **The wall is the largest surface in frame and carries the least information** — flat matte lilac with no paper texture, no scuff, no chair rail, no outlet, no switch, no door. Meanwhile the floor grain is high-frequency and crisp. Inconsistent detail density; §4 #25, #79.
8. **The wire basket reads as a wireframe** — unlit thin rods with visible aliasing and no contents. Weakest prop in frame.
9. **The shelf books are all the same height class, all perfectly vertical, none leaning, none pulled forward, no gap.** §4 #80.
10. **Frame-right is a thicket** — the chair, table and two stools are clipped by the edge and their leg lines tangent the rug's ellipse. §4 #111.
11. The window that motivates the key is almost entirely out of frame, so the large lit patch on the floor has no visible source. §4 #43, borderline.
12. A bright orange bloom corona traces the baby's head (see D6).

---

### `02-room-wide-hud` — same frame, HUD on

Adds the UI. See `40-play-blocks` for the detailed UI read; two things are specific to this framing:

13. **The bottom UI band plus the prompt bubble consume the entire lower third**, cropping the rug and covering the toys. The prompt reads「ボールを ころころ！」("roll the ball") with a downward arrow — but the ball is at frame-left and the arrow points at the *blocks*. The instruction and the affordance disagree.
14. **The meter panel top-left is a hard white rectangle that terminates in a flat vertical cut** at x≈475 with square-ish bottom corners — a corner-radius language inconsistent with the heavily rounded activity tiles below it. §4 #120.
15. **A numeric "0" sits in the top-right corner** beside a star. That is the conventional score position and reads as a score. The contract forbids scores; a sticker/star *count* is defensible, but it is not currently distinguished from one.

---

### `03-baby-face` — hero portrait, `play` / `face`

**This is the frame the shot list calls the hero face closeup, and it is the worst frame in the build.**

16. **There is no nose and no mouth.** Approximately 45% of the head's vertical extent — everything below the eyes — is a featureless expanse of pink. No nostrils, no philtrum, no lip line, no mouth aperture, no chin crease. The geometry exists in source (`anatomy.js:125` places a 12×10×17.5 mm nose ellipsoid; `anatomy.js:377–390` place a philtrum groove, a lip-line groove and mouth-corner dimples) — but `BodyField` runs at `k = 100`, an ~10 mm fillet radius, against a cranium of ~120 mm radius. **The smooth-union fillet is the same order as the nose, so the nose is absorbed into the skull.** The grooves at 2.6–5.2 mm depth then read as nothing on a matte, SSS-lifted surface. §4 #14, and it is the direct cause of C1 and C4 collapsing.
17. **The two eyes look like different eyes.** Frame-left is a pale milky-grey lens with two soft blobs and no iris visible at all. Frame-right shows a dark navy iris with a hard white speck. They are not converged — they are *divergent*. Root cause below (D3).
18. **Eyebrows are opaque hard-edged wedges pasted on the skin** — no root fade, no strand breakup, no brow ridge beneath, and angled down-and-inward so the resting expression reads *stern*. Real infant brows are barely present. The right brow is longer, thicker and darker than the left in a way that reads as a bug, not authored asymmetry.
19. **The crown hair is a hard-edged grey/olive/white banded strip** with visible light/dark striping — it reads as untextured or back-facing cards, not hair. §4 #15, #138.
20. **A grey diamond-crosshatch patch with a hard boundary sits on the baby's right upper arm** at approximately (280–400, 610–720). It looks like a fishnet decal. This is a placeholder-grade artefact and it recurs in three further frames. §4 #138.
21. **Skin reads as oiled vinyl.** Uniform high-saturation salmon with no value differentiation between forehead, cheek and jaw; no visible pore detail even at this scale; no roughness breakup; a broad greasy clearcoat sheen across forehead, cheek and chest. `happy` sets `blush: 0.28` and **no blush is visible** (see D5). §4 #21, #19, #60, #61.
22. **A hard faceted seam runs down the chest** at x≈560, y 560–700, and another where the shoulder shell meets the torso at x 830–960. Visible polygon facets and a hard crease. §4 #2.
23. **The right cranium silhouette is visibly faceted** — the flat segments are countable at x≈960, y 250–420. §4 #5.
24. **Insufficient headroom.** The crown sits ~40px from the top edge and the arm exits frame-left. §4 #112, #113. `camera.js` `face` preset targets `[0.025, 0.315, 0]` — chest height, not eye height, which is why the head rides high.
25. **RGB fringing is visible along the rug's top silhouette edge** at frame-right — chromatic aberration landing on a high-contrast edge in mid-frame, not just at the corners.

---

### `04`, `06` — not captured (time budget). Not scored.

### `05-baby-cry` — `cry` at full intensity, `closeup`

The `cry` mood sets `browSad: 1.0, mouthCry: 1.0, jawOpen: 0.62, lidClose: 0.80, tears: 1.0, noseWrinkle: 0.40, blush: 0.55`. What actually renders:

26. **`cry` and `happy` are visually indistinguishable except that a small pink oval opens.** The mouth is a tic-tac-shaped lozenge roughly 1/8 the face width, low and slightly off the centreline, with no lips, no lip line, no visible throat depth, no teeth, no tension. A full-intensity cry should be a wide, tall, tense rectangle.
27. **`browSad: 1.0` produces no change.** The brows are pixel-for-pixel the same flat straight pose as in `03-baby-face`. §4 #57 — only the mouth changes.
28. **`lidClose: 0.80` produces no change.** The eyes are as open as in the happy frame.
29. **`tears: 1.0` produces nothing.** No tears, no wet eyes, no tear track.
30. **`blush: 0.55` produces no visible cheek colour.** See D5 — the decal peaks at 0.32 opacity, which is imperceptible over this skin under this key.
31. **The pose is identical to `07-baby-full`** — same sit, same arm angles, same leg positions — despite the emotional state being at maximum. A crying infant is tense, arched, arms up. Nothing about the body responds to mood.
32. **The teal/grey artefact patches recur** on the right upper arm (600–640, 600–640) and the left hip (845–875, 685–720). Confirmed persistent, not per-frame noise.

**Emotion is not legible with the UI hidden and audio off.** That is the C4 1/5 anchor, verbatim.

---

### `07-baby-full` — full body, `play` / `closeup`

33. **Both eyes are blank white lozenges — no iris, no pupil, in either eye.** The character reads as blind. This is now confirmed in three separate frames at three head angles.
34. **No mouth, no nose.** Confirmed at a second angle.
35. **Proportions.** Head-to-body reads about 1:3 seated, which is inside the rubric's target band, and the thigh ring-creases from `anatomy.js` *are* visible and are a genuine win. But the arms are boneless smooth tubes attaching low and far back, with no elbow, no wrist, and a paddle for a hand — no fingers. Feet are lumps with no toes. Belly protrudes well past the chest, shoulders are narrow and sloped. Net read: inflatable vinyl doll, not infant. §4 #16, #17-adjacent.
36. **Two hard-edged coloured artefact patches on the body** (teal on the right arm, teal-grey on the left hip) plus the grey banded crown strip. §4 #138.
37. **A hard polygon crease down the chest** where the shoulder shell meets the torso. §4 #2.
38. **The rug at this distance reads as uniform salt-and-pepper stipple** with no larger-scale structure — noise masquerading as detail, the exact thing the brief asked me to hunt.
39. **A hard-edged crimson disc intrudes at frame-left** (the drum, blown and clipped by the edge) with a stray blue sliver at its base and visible aliasing on its rim.
40. **The cast shadow is real and correctly directed** — genuinely good — **but there is no contact hardening.** The shadow is equally soft directly under the buttocks and two feet away. `contactShadow()` exists in `lighting.js` for exactly this and is not doing the job here. §4 #36.
41. **The bloom corona is the brightest, most attention-grabbing event in the frame** — it rings the head and shoulders in orange. §4 #102.

### `21-bath-foam` — `bath` / `tub`, water 0.8, foam 0.9, bubbles on

**The subject is absent.** The tub is empty: no baby, no water surface, no foam, no bubbles. The black polygon covers the tub interior, so I cannot separate "occluded" from "not emitting" and I score nothing on that. Everything outside the tub interior is assessable:

42. **There is a rainbow gradient bar with a small grey sphere on it, applied to the front face of the tub.** It reads unambiguously as a debug colour ramp or a mis-scaled UI widget pasted onto 3D geometry. It is the single most damaging *prop* detail in the build. §4 #138, #133.
43. **A stray white sphere floats in the void** at approximately (578, 133) with nothing attaching it to anything. §4 #138.
44. **The wastebasket at frame-left has a countable diagonal weave repeat** and the pattern stretches visibly at the rim. Its rim silhouette has ~24 countable flat segments and a hard unbevelled edge catching a bright specular. §4 #24, #26, #5, #1.
45. **The tub rests on its stand with a visible intersection** — the shell passes through the top rails. Two unexplained grey nubs hang below the front. §4 #2, #3.
46. **The bathmat at bottom-centre is a flat card.** No perceptible thickness at the near edge, no pile, no fringe, no fold, no contact shadow. §4 #83, #13.
47. **The floor plank grain repeat is now plainly countable** — identical curved grain arcs recur across planks in the lower-left quadrant. §4 #24.
48. **The side table is four dowels and a slab with a hard 90° edge and no apron.** §4 #1.
49. **Shadows are uniformly soft with no contact hardening** and are neutral grey-brown with no cool sky tint, despite `evening` specifying a cool `fillColor: 0xb8c8f0`. §4 #36, #41.
50. **The whole frame has gone chalky.** The `evening` mood lands as muddy grey-lilac against beige. It is the least attractive frame of the set.
51. **No focal point, subject dead-centre, lower-left third is empty floor.** §4 #136, #109.

**Genuinely good in this frame:** the soap pump bottle (proper neck, shoulder, plausible plastic sheen) and the two stacked soap bars with rounded edges are the best-resolved small props in the build.

---

### `30-dress-outfit` — `dress` / `closeup`, HUD on

**The frame contains an empty rug, a floor, and the UI. No baby. No wardrobe. No outfits. No customisation row.** The prompt reads「すきな およふくを えらんでね」("choose the clothes you like") with a downward arrow pointing at nothing.

52. **Root cause, confirmed in code:** `dress.js:95` places the activity root at `ctx.room.anchor('wardrobe')`. `ACTIVITIES.dress.camera = 'closeup'`, and `camera.js` `closeup` is a **hardcoded absolute world position** `pos [0.46, 0.55, 0.78] / target [-0.03, 0.30, 0]`. The camera never looks at the wardrobe. Every `BUILTIN` preset in `camera.js` is absolute-world and only correct when the subject is at the origin. This is a structural defect, not a tuning one. (D1)
53. Also visible: the rug shows **low-frequency blotchy mottling and a soft banded gradient** across its centre, and a hard edge against the floor with no pile transition.

---

### `40-play-blocks` — `play` / `floor`, HUD on

**The UI in this frame is the second-best thing in the build.**

**What works.** Five activity tiles at the bottom, custom-drawn vector icons (bottle, bathtub, onesie, balloon, moon) — **no emoji anywhere**, which retires §4 #119 and the rubric's §4.11 top offender. Consistent stroke weight, consistent rounded-square tiles, consistent soft drop shadow, a clear selected state (warm yellow, lifted, with a contrasting label chip). Exactly five choices — at the top of the Toca Boca 3–5 band, not over it. Icons are *literal* pictures of the thing. The prompt「つみきを ぽん！」carries a blocks icon and a directional arrow. `hud.css` is a real token system (`--r-pill`, `--sh-1/2/3`, `--t-fast`, `--ease`, `--blur`, per-meter gradient pairs). It looks like one designer made all of it.

**What is wrong.**

54. **The prompt bubble sits directly over the block tower** — it occludes the exact object it is instructing the child to tap. Functional failure as well as compositional. §4 #117-adjacent, #132-adjacent.
55. **The meter icons are ~20px and the labels ~12px.** At a child's viewing distance the apple reads as a red blob and the labels are invisible. Icon literalism collapses below a size threshold.
56. **Meters are pill rectangles with four different fill ramps over one identical grey track.** No tick, no face, no material, no personality. Close to §4 #124.
57. **The UI is cold pure-white flat vector over a warm lilac-and-honey 3D world, drawn at full sharpness over a DoF-softened scene with no depth relationship.** It reads as a decal layer, not as an object in the nursery. §4 #133, #125 (partial).
58. **The bottom row spans the full frame width and crowds the bottom edge** — the ねんね label pill sits ~25px from the frame boundary. §4 #128.
59. **Only three blocks are stacked; the state requested `stack: 5`.** Two are missing.
60. **The tower intersects the baby's forearm** at approximately (630–660, 600–680). §4 #2, #3.
61. **The blocks are not grounded to each other** — a clean lit gap shows between each block's base and the one below. No inter-block contact shadow or AO. §4 #34.
62. **The block symbols are dark inset shapes that read as holes**, not carved or painted marks, and the flower motif repeats identically at identical rotation on two visible faces. §4 #12.
63. **Block edges are hard 90°** with no micro-bevel and no specular line. §4 #1.
64. **The balloon's specular is three or four hard-edged white blobs stuck to the surface** — painted decals, not reflections.
65. **The xylophone behind the baby is a near-black slab** — completely lost in shadow, unreadable.
66. **Chromatic fringing on the drum at frame-left** (hard red rim) and along the rug/floor boundary at frame-right.
67. **Baby: blank white eyes, no mouth, no nose, naked, bloom corona.** Fourth confirmation.

---

### `51-sleep-asleep` — `sleep` / `face`, lamp on. **100% black frame.**

The shot list calls this "the money shot for lighting." It renders as a uniformly black 1440×900 image.

68. **Independent root cause, confirmed in code, separate from the light-shaft polygon.** `sleep.js:1040` calls `cameraRig.goTo('face')`. `camera.js` `face` is at world `y = 0.44` with target `y = 0.315`. `props.js:436` puts the crib mattress base at `low + 0.03 = 0.45` m with side rails at 0.71 and 0.90 m, and the crib is placed at an anchor away from the origin. **The camera is below the mattress plane and inside the cot frame, aimed at nothing.** Combined with the `night` mood's low exposure the result is black. This must be fixed for the shot to be assessable at all, whatever happens to the light shaft. (D2)
69. **Consequence: the `night` lighting mood is entirely unevaluated.** No score in this review reflects it.

---

### `61-golden-hour` — `play`, golden mood

**No character in frame.** Room only.

70. **As rendered, `golden` is barely distinguishable from `day` and has lost almost all its cast shadow.** The pouf has a faint shadow; the stools, table and chair have essentially none. Compare `01-room-wide` (day, same polygon occlusion) where floor shadows are strong and directional. Golden hour means a low warm raking key throwing long shadows; this reads as flat ambient. The `MOODS.golden` preset in `lighting.js` *is* a genuinely distinct setup on paper (different key colour, position, intensity, rim) — the frame is not delivering it.
71. **The rug is a painted bullseye.** Three perfectly concentric, perfectly centred circles. No wear, no directional pile, no flattening under traffic, no fringe. Hard elliptical boundary with no thickness and no perimeter contact shadow. §4 #83, #7, #135.
72. **A small dark puncture mark sits at the rug's exact centre** (≈658, 700) — stray vertex or decal artefact. §4 #138.
73. **The table top's wood grain is a radial starburst emanating from the dead centre**, repeated on both stools. No real timber does this; it is a rotationally-symmetric procedural giving itself away. §4 #31, #7.
74. **The curtain is a set of parallel vertical folds of exactly equal width, depth and spacing.** §4 #7, #135.
75. **Every slat edge on the chair catches a hard bright specular line from an unbevelled 90° edge.** §4 #1 — textbook.
76. **Visible vertical mottling/streaking on the wall** at x 200–320 near the curtain — low-frequency texture noise reading as dirt.
77. **Chromatic fringing** (magenta/green) along the chair's frame-right edge and the top of the pouf.
78. **No subject, no focal point.** §4 #136.

---

### `62-clutter` — `play`, `Room.clutter(true)`

**The room genuinely does read more lived-in with clutter on. This should be the default state.** That said:

79. **The scatter is statistically uniform.** ~14 items spread at near-constant spacing across the rug and floor. No clusters, no piles, no two objects touching, none stacked, none against a wall or under furniture, none half-on the rug edge. Real clutter clumps and drifts to edges. §4 #73.
80. **Every clutter cube presents a flat top face parallel to the floor and a face square to camera.** Not one is tipped onto a corner or an edge. §4 #12, #80, #8.
81. **Two visually inconsistent block assets coexist in one room.** The clutter cubes are plain rounded blocks with *no* symbol insets; the tower blocks in `40-play-blocks` have embossed symbols. Same object, two looks.
82. **The clutter shadow under the yellow block at bottom-centre-left is offset from the block** — peter-panning. §4 #38. Several items on the wooden floor at frame-right have shadows so diffuse they read as smudges rather than shadows. §4 #36. Note `room.js:403` constructs the clutter contact shadow as `contactShadow(1.7, 0.0, 2.6)` — **opacity 0.0**.
83. **The balls are plain matte spheres with a faintly faceted silhouette.** §4 #5.

## 2. The 16-category score table

| # | Category | W | Score | One-line justification |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| C1 | Character appeal & proportions | 10 | **2** | Baby schema is present at silhouette level and the thigh creases are real, but the face has no nose and no mouth, arms are boneless tubes with no elbow and mitten hands with no fingers, and hard boolean seams show at the shoulder and chest. |
| C2 | Skin shading & subsurface feel | 8 | **2** | A real wrap+backscatter SSS shader with a warm ramp exists and the terminator is soft — but as rendered the skin is uniform saturated salmon with a greasy clearcoat sheen, no roughness variation, and no blush at any mood. Reads as painted vinyl. |
| C3 | Eyes & gaze | 9 | **1** | In 4 of 5 face-bearing frames one or both irises are rolled entirely out of view and the eye renders as a blank white lozenge; the one visible iris is divergent, not converged; the catchlight is a fixed unlit additive billboard that ignores the key light. |
| C4 | Facial expression range | 7 | **1** | `cry` at full intensity is indistinguishable from `happy` except that a small oval opens — brows, lids, tears and blush all produce no visible change. Emotion is not legible with UI hidden. This is the 1/5 anchor verbatim. |
| C5 | Hair | 6 | **1** | Renders as a hard-edged grey/olive banded strip on the crown that reads as broken or back-facing cards, plus a stray crosshatch patch on the arm. No strand breakup, no anisotropic highlight, no hairline blend. |
| C6 | Cloth & material believability | 7 | **2** | Environment material families are genuinely distinct and correct (grained wood, piped plush, quilted mattress, ceramic, wire, plastic) — but the character wears nothing in any frame, the wastebasket shows countable tiling and stretched UVs, and unbevelled 90° edges are everywhere. |
| C7 | Animation quality & secondary motion | 10 | **2*** | *Provisional — stills only.* Pose is byte-identical between `happy` and full-intensity `cry`, so the body does not respond to mood; and a code check confirms nothing in `anim.js`/`baby.js` ever schedules an unprompted `gesture()`, so the 11 authored idle gestures never fire autonomously. |
| C8 | Environment richness & set dressing | 8 | **3** | Properly built room with real architecture, ~25 distinct props, and shadows on every object — squarely the 3/5 anchor. Held there by total axis-alignment, uniform clutter scatter, a showroom tidiness, and an information-free wall. |
| C9 | Lighting & mood | 9 | **3** | Four genuinely distinct mood setups, warm key vs cool fill, rim, procedural PMREM env, GTAO, real value range with true darks and brights. Held at 3 by absent contact hardening, a character that is not the brightest element in the wide shot, and a blown bloom corona on the subject. |
| C10 | Colour grading & post-processing | 6 | **3** | AgX in-pass with per-mood lift/gain/sat/contrast, threshold bloom, vignette, grain-as-dither, SMAA — no banding, no clipping, coherent palette. Held at 3 because the bloom threshold is not actually holding on skin and CA fringes mid-frame edges. |

| C12 | Particle & FX craft | 6 | **n/a** | **Not scored.** Zero particles visible in any frame, including one that explicitly requests foam and bubbles. Cannot separate "not emitting" from "occluded." Filed as defect D14. |
| C13 | UI/HUD visual design | 7 | **3** | Custom vector icons with no emoji, a real CSS token system, consistent tiles and a clear selected state — it looks like one designer made all of it.
```
Weighted mean:      1.98 / 5   (over the 15 scored categories, total weight 118)
Unweighted mean:    2.00 / 5   (15 scored)
Floor rule applied: yes — C3, C4, C5, C16 = 1 and seven more ≤ 2, capping the
                    headline at 3.4. The weighted mean is below the cap, so
                    the cap is not binding.
HEADLINE:           1.98 / 5
```

**Top 3 highest-leverage fixes (biggest score delta per unit of effort):**

1. **Fix the eye-gaze coordinate-frame mismatch (D3).** One coordinate-space bug is costing the entire C3 category (weight 9) and most of C16. The eye pivots are parented to `this.group` but the gaze target is converted into `head` bone space — the eyes are pinned at the pitch clamp with the irises rolled out of view. Half a day, moves C3 from 1 to 3+.
2. **Make the face have a face (D4).** Raise the smooth-union `k` locally around the nose, or add the nose as a post-smoothing additive displacement, and deepen the lip-line groove enough to read under SSS. Currently the 10 mm fillet radius eats a 12 mm nose. This unblocks C1, C4, C14 and C16 simultaneously.
3. **Make camera presets subject-relative (D1).** Every `BUILTIN` preset is an absolute world position valid only at the origin. Fixing this recovers `30-dress-outfit`, `51-sleep-asleep`, and probably `21-bath-foam` — three dead frames from one change, and it is the largest single contributor to C11.

**Single worst thing in the frame:**

The baby has no face. In every frame that shows the head, there is no nose, no mouth, and two blank white eyes. The entire product is a caretaking game about a character, and the character's face — the one surface a 4-year-old reads to know how the baby feels — is a smooth pink blank. Nothing else on this list matters until that is fixed.

Result: `30-dress-outfit` frames empty rug; `21-bath-foam` frames an empty tub. | `src/engine/camera.js` `BUILTIN`; `src/activities/*.js` | Presets stored as offsets resolved against a subject transform at `goTo()` time (baby root, or the activity root). Every one of the nine presets frames its subject regardless of where the activity places it. |

A dedicated `crib-face` preset resolved off the crib anchor. |
| **D3** | **Coordinate-frame mismatch in the gaze solver.** `attach()` (`face.js:531`) parents `this.group` to the head bone and offsets it by `-headBone.getWorldPosition()`, so `this.group` is in *bind-world* space. Eye pivots are added to `this.group` at bind-world coordinates `(±0.030, 0.5320, 0.0530)` (`face.js:392–394`). But `_updateGaze` converts the look target with `head.worldToLocal(...)` (`face.js:611`, `:623`) — **head-bone-local** space, which differs from `this.group` by that same ~0.5 m offset. `dy = localTarget.y - p.y` (`face.js:629`) is therefore ~0.5 m too negative, driving `pitch` to the `-0.42` rad clamp permanently. Both irises roll out of the lid aperture and the eyes render as blank white lozenges in `07`, `40`, `62` and one eye in `03`. | `src/character/face.js` `_updateGaze` (`:605–651`) | Either convert the target into `this.group` space (`this.group.worldToLocal`) or offset `p` by the attach shift. ## 4. Verdict

### Would this beat the reference in a blind A/B on a single still?

**No. Not on any frame currently in `docs/review/`, and not close.**

I must restate that I have never seen the reference. What follows is reasoning against the rubric's own written characterisation of it (§1, §0.3): a competent, low-budget, shipped console family title whose weaknesses are flat lighting, uniform materials, sparse modular set dressing, fixed forward gaze, a small discrete expression set and generic UI — and whose strength is that it is a *finished, coherent product* with a complete rigged character.

The reference's floor is "the baby has a face, wears clothes, and is visible in the shot." This build is currently below that floor. Of eleven frames:

- **Four contain no usable subject at all** — one is 100% black, one is an empty rug, one is an empty tub, one is an empty room.
- **Five show the character**, and in all five he has no nose, no mouth, blank white eyes, and no clothes.
- **Two** (`01-room-wide`, `62-clutter`) are genuinely competitive frames — and in both, the character is a 7%-of-frame pink blank that the eye skips over on its way to the furniture.

A parent shown `03-baby-face` for three seconds would think *"something is wrong with that baby's face."* That is not a craft deficit that a lighting pass closes.

### What is holding it back

The gap is **not** where the rubric predicted, and this is the single most useful finding in the review. The rubric's §4.11 calibration list — emoji as art, no shadows anywhere, compressed value range, box room, primitive-recognisable forms — is **substantially retired**. There are no emoji. Every object casts a shadow. The value range is real. The room is properly built with ~25 props. The material families are distinct. The tone-mapping and grade stack is a 4/5 stack. The UI icon set is custom-drawn and disciplined. On paper, the systems in `lighting.js`, `render.js`, `materials.js`, `camera.js` and `fx.js` are aiming at the 5/5 anchors, not the 3/5 ones.

What is holding it back is that **a small number of hard bugs are hiding all of that work**, and they are concentrated on the character and the camera:

1. **One coordinate-frame bug in `face.js` blinds the character.** (D3)
2. **One smoothing parameter in `anatomy.js` erases the nose and mouth.** (D4)
3. **One structural assumption in `camera.js` — that presets are absolute world positions — kills four frames.** (D1, D2)
4. **One default-state omission leaves the baby naked in every shot.** (D8)
5. **One shader gain in `makeSkin` blows the bloom threshold and wraps the character in an orange halo.** (D6)

Those five are, between them, most of the distance from 1.98 to something in the 3s. They are all bugs, not art direction. That is the good news in this report and the reason the headline number understates the build's actual position.

The **art-direction** gap — the distance from 3 to 4/5 — is a separate and much longer list, and it is the one the rubric predicted correctly: everything in this room is level, square, clean, evenly spaced and unworn. Nothing is tilted, nothing is half-off anything, no two instances of the same prop differ, no edge is bevelled, no surface is worn, and there is nothing anywhere that rewards a second look. §4 #134 — *clean but sterile* — is the accurate one-line summary of the environment once the bugs are gone. That is the work after Tier 1.

### Two things to protect

Regressions here would be the most expensive kind:

- **The room shell and prop set** (`world/props.js`, `world/room.js`). It is the strongest asset in the build and it is already at the 3/5 anchor with a clear path to 4.
- **The UI icon set and CSS token system** (`ui/icons.js`, `ui/hud.css`). No emoji, literal icons, five choices, one consistent visual language. This category was capped at 1 in the rubric's own calibration pass and is now a legitimate 3.
